messages.content:
# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

messages.content:
# The database

shortlink keeps everything in one SQLite file. The `database` setting
names it (`shortlink.db` by default) and can be overridden with the
`DATABASE` environment variable. The container image keeps its database
in the /data volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` there. SQLite
runs in WAL mode. All storage goes through `internal/store`.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |

## Tables

| Table | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| links | Every link: its short code, target URL, creation time, and expiry time |
| clicks_daily | Daily click counts per link, kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days by default) |
| api_keys | API keys by name and scope, plus revocation state and each key's SHA-256 hash |
| schema_version | Which migrations have been applied to this file |

Only the hash of an API key is stored, never the key itself. A link's
target cannot be changed after the link is created; delete the link and
create it again with the same slug.

## Migrations

Since v1.3.0 migrations run automatically when the server starts. The
`shortlink migrate` command applies them by hand and exits:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Use it to migrate without starting the server, and when upgrading from
v1.2.0 or earlier: those databases predate automatic migrations, so run
`shortlink migrate` with the new binary before starting it.

Migrations only go forward. Downgrading after a migration is not
supported; restore a backup instead. Back up before every upgrade.

## One process per database file

Run one shortlink process per database file. A second process pointed at
the same file fails with "database is locked". If you need more than one
instance, give each its own `database` file.

## Supported databases

SQLite is the only supported database. The file named by `database` is
the whole datastore.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file, but copying it directly can catch
it partway through a write. Back it up with the SQLite backup command
while the server runs:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

Back up the database before every upgrade, and before running
`shortlink migrate` by hand. If an upgrade or a migration has to be
undone, stop the server and put the backup back in place as the database
file; run one process per database file as usual.

# The admin page

The admin page is a read-only view of the links in the database. It is
off by default and lives at /admin on `listen_addr` (`:8080` by
default). It arrived in v1.4.0.

## Turning it on

Set `admin.enabled` in config/defaults.yaml, or override it with an
environment variable of the same name in capitals:

```yaml
admin:
  enabled: true
```

```sh
ADMIN_ENABLED=true shortlink serve
```

Run `shortlink check-config` to confirm the configuration loads.

## Setting the password

`admin.password_hash` is not written by hand. Run this on the server
and enter the password at the prompt:

```sh
shortlink admin set-password
```

The command stores the hash in `admin.password_hash`. shortlink keeps
only the hash, so the password cannot be recovered from the
configuration. Run the command again to change the password.

## What it shows

Everything on the page is read-only. You can:

- Search links.
- See each link's daily click counts.

You cannot create, edit, or delete links there. To change links, use
the JSON API or the `shortlink links` commands; see api.md. Daily click
counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default), so the
page does not show counts older than that.

## Logging in

Sign in with the password set by `shortlink admin set-password`. A login
lasts 12 hours, after which you sign in again.

## Protecting /admin

The page is served on `listen_addr` under /admin, the same port as
redirects and the API, so it is reachable wherever that port is
reachable. Put it behind the access controls of your reverse proxy as
well, for example HTTP basic auth or an IP allowlist in nginx or Caddy.
See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

If you also run shortlink behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For,
list the proxy in `trusted_proxies` so rate limiting sees the real
client address.

## Example

```yaml
listen_addr: :8080
database: shortlink.db
admin:
  enabled: true
  password_hash: "$2a$10$..."   # set by `shortlink admin set-password`
```

Then start the server and open http://localhost:8080/admin.

# Rate limits

Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

A client over its limit gets 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After
header giving the number of seconds to wait. Redirects count against
the limit too, so a link shared widely from one office network can
exhaust that network's limit.

# Troubleshooting

## A new link returns 404

If the link was created with an expires_at time that has already
passed, it is expired from the moment it is created, and its short URL
returns 404. Check the expires_at value, including its time zone.

## Every user hits the rate limit at once

shortlink is probably behind a proxy and sees every request as coming
from the proxy's address. Set trusted_proxies; see deploy.md.

## "database is locked"

Two shortlink processes are using the same SQLite file. Run one process
per database file.

# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

message.content:
You don't need to raise the limits — the problem is that shortlink is treating every visitor as one client. Per **docs/troubleshooting.md** and **docs/deploy.md**, this happens when shortlink sits behind a reverse proxy: all requests arrive from the proxy's address, so everyone shares a single per-IP budget and hits the limit together.

## What to set

Set **trusted_proxies** to the address(es) of your reverse proxy (nginx, HAProxy, etc.). Once a request comes from a listed proxy, shortlink takes the real client address from the `X-Forwarded-For` header the proxy adds, and each user gets their own limit again.

For example, if nginx runs on the same machine as shortlink:

```yaml
# config/defaults.yaml (override)
trusted_proxies:
  - 127.0.0.1
```

or as an environment variable (**docs/configuration.md**: settings become capitals, dots become underscores):

```bash
export TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1
```

If the proxy is on another host, list that host's address instead (e.g. `10.0.0.5`). Include every proxy in the chain if there is more than one.

Then verify without starting the server:

```bash
shortlink check-config
```

## Notes

- The limits themselves are `rate_limit.requests_per_minute` (120) and `rate_limit.burst` (20) — **docs/rate-limits.md** — and each client is identified by IP, so redirects count against the limit too. Only raise those if genuine individual users still exceed 120 requests/minute after fixing trusted_proxies.
- Only list proxies you control; shortlink believes the `X-Forwarded-For` header from those addresses (**docs/configuration.md**), so a wrong entry lets clients spoof their IP.

messages.content:
# The admin page

The admin page is a read-only view of the links in the database. It is
off by default and lives at /admin on `listen_addr` (`:8080` by
default). It arrived in v1.4.0.

## Turning it on

Set `admin.enabled` in config/defaults.yaml, or override it with an
environment variable of the same name in capitals:

```yaml
admin:
  enabled: true
```

```sh
ADMIN_ENABLED=true shortlink serve
```

Run `shortlink check-config` to confirm the configuration loads.

## Setting the password

`admin.password_hash` is not written by hand. Run this on the server
and enter the password at the prompt:

```sh
shortlink admin set-password
```

The command stores the hash in `admin.password_hash`. shortlink keeps
only the hash, so the password cannot be recovered from the
configuration. Run the command again to change the password.

## What it shows

Everything on the page is read-only. You can:

- Search links.
- See each link's daily click counts.

You cannot create, edit, or delete links there. To change links, use
the JSON API or the `shortlink links` commands; see api.md. Daily click
counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default), so the
page does not show counts older than that.

## Logging in

Sign in with the password set by `shortlink admin set-password`. A login
lasts 12 hours, after which you sign in again.

## Protecting /admin

The page is served on `listen_addr` under /admin, the same port as
redirects and the API, so it is reachable wherever that port is
reachable. Put it behind the access controls of your reverse proxy as
well, for example HTTP basic auth or an IP allowlist in nginx or Caddy.
See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

If you also run shortlink behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For,
list the proxy in `trusted_proxies` so rate limiting sees the real
client address.

## Example

```yaml
listen_addr: :8080
database: shortlink.db
admin:
  enabled: true
  password_hash: "$2a$10$..."   # set by `shortlink admin set-password`
```

Then start the server and open http://localhost:8080/admin.

# The database

shortlink keeps everything in one SQLite file. The `database` setting
names it (`shortlink.db` by default) and can be overridden with the
`DATABASE` environment variable. The container image keeps its database
in the /data volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` there. SQLite
runs in WAL mode. All storage goes through `internal/store`.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |

## Tables

| Table | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| links | Every link: its short code, target URL, creation time, and expiry time |
| clicks_daily | Daily click counts per link, kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days by default) |
| api_keys | API keys by name and scope, plus revocation state and each key's SHA-256 hash |
| schema_version | Which migrations have been applied to this file |

Only the hash of an API key is stored, never the key itself. A link's
target cannot be changed after the link is created; delete the link and
create it again with the same slug.

## Migrations

Since v1.3.0 migrations run automatically when the server starts. The
`shortlink migrate` command applies them by hand and exits:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Use it to migrate without starting the server, and when upgrading from
v1.2.0 or earlier: those databases predate automatic migrations, so run
`shortlink migrate` with the new binary before starting it.

Migrations only go forward. Downgrading after a migration is not
supported; restore a backup instead. Back up before every upgrade.

## One process per database file

Run one shortlink process per database file. A second process pointed at
the same file fails with "database is locked". If you need more than one
instance, give each its own `database` file.

## Supported databases

SQLite is the only supported database. The file named by `database` is
the whole datastore.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file, but copying it directly can catch
it partway through a write. Back it up with the SQLite backup command
while the server runs:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

Back up the database before every upgrade, and before running
`shortlink migrate` by hand. If an upgrade or a migration has to be
undone, stop the server and put the backup back in place as the database
file; run one process per database file as usual.

List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. That address is what rate limiting and request logs use, so only trust proxies you control.

## API keys

Create keys only on the server, with the narrowest scope that works:

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

A key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash, so a lost key cannot be recovered; create a new one and revoke the old one with `shortlink keys revoke <id>`. Treat keys like passwords: pass them in the Authorization header and keep them out of source control and shell history.

Scopes are read (GET requests), write (also create and delete links), and admin (also read every link's clicks across the server). A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

The admin password is separate from API keys. Set it with `shortlink admin set-password`, which stores its hash; a login lasts 12 hours.

## Target URLs

Targets must be http or https URLs no longer than max_url_length (2048 bytes). Refuse whole domains when you create links by listing them in blocked_domains; a link to one of those domains is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked". The check runs when a link is created, so review blocked_domains before importing links in bulk with `shortlink links import`.

The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved and can't be used as slugs. A slug already in use gets 409 Conflict.

With redirect_status 302 (the default), deleting a link or letting it expire stops the redirect at once. With 301, browsers cache the target and keep going there even after the link is deleted or expires. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## Metrics and the admin page

Prometheus metrics are served on metrics_addr (`:9090` by default), on a separate port from listen_addr. Keep that port off the public internet: bind it to a private interface or block it at the firewall. Set metrics_addr to an empty value to turn metrics off.

The admin page is off by default (admin.enabled false). It is read-only, but it shows links and their daily clicks, so put it behind the proxy's access controls as well as its own password. It is served on listen_addr under /admin.

## Webhook signing

If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. # Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

# Architecture

## Code layout

shortlink is one binary. Each part of it lives in its own package under `internal/`, except for the entry point:

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/shortlink` | Entry point. Parses the command line, loads configuration, opens the database, applies migrations, and starts the server. `shortlink` with no command runs `shortlink serve`. |
| `internal/store` | SQLite storage. Owns the `links`, `clicks_daily`, `api_keys`, and `schema_version` tables and the database file (`shortlink.db` by default) in WAL mode. |
| `internal/redirect` | Resolves short codes and answers redirects with `redirect_status`, applying `append_query` to the target. |
| `internal/api` | The JSON API under `/api`, and the request checks that go with it: URL length, `blocked_domains`, slug rules. |
| `internal/limit` | Per-client rate limiting: `rate_limit.requests_per_minute` with `rate_limit.burst` on top. |
| `internal/clicks` | Click counting. Holds counts in memory and writes them to `clicks_daily`. |
| `internal/hooks` | Webhooks: signing, delivery, and retries. |
| `internal/admin` | The read-only admin page served at `/admin`. |

The same process also answers `/healthz` and, on `metrics_addr`, `/metrics`. Migrations run automatically when the server starts; `shortlink migrate` applies them by hand.

## A redirect request

1. `internal/limit` rates the client. The client address comes from the connection, or from the `X-Forwarded-For` header when the peer is listed in `trusted_proxies` (see docs/deploy.md). Over the limit returns 429 and increments `shortlink_rate_limited_total`.
2. `internal/redirect` looks the code up in the in-memory cache, if `cache_size` is not 0. A hit adds to `shortlink_cache_hits_total`, a miss to `shortlink_cache_misses_total`, and the miss falls through to the database.
3. `internal/store` returns the link. A missing code, a reserved code (`api`, `admin`, `healthz`, `metrics`), or a link past its `expires_at` returns 404.
4. `internal/redirect` answers with `redirect_status` (302 by default) and, with `append_query` true, copies the short URL's query string onto the target. A `HEAD` request gets the same answer as `GET` but goes no further: no click is counted.
5. `internal/clicks` adds one click to its in-memory counts, bots included. Counts are written to `clicks_daily` every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds), so a new click appears in the API within about 5 seconds and a crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts. A normal shutdown flushes first.

## An API request

1. `internal/limit` rates the client as for a redirect.
2. `internal/api` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header and asks `internal/store` to match it against the `api_keys` table. The store compares the SHA-256 hash of the presented key. A missing, wrong, or revoked key is 401; a valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request is 403.
3. The key's scope decides what is allowed: `read` for GET, `write` for creating and deleting links, `admin` for reading every link's clicks across the server.
4. The handler validates the body in `internal/api`: targets must be `http` or `https` and no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), a domain in `blocked_domains` is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked", a `slug` is 3 to 32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens, and a slug already in use is 409 Conflict. Codes are generated by the store at `code_length` from letters and digits, minus `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, and `I`.
5. `internal/store` writes or reads the link. A link's target cannot be changed: delete it and create it again with the same slug.
6. For `link.created` and `link.deleted`, `internal/hooks` POSTs a JSON body to `webhooks.url` when that setting is set. Each request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. Delivery failures are retried up to 5 attempts in all, waiting 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s between them; after the last failure the event is logged and dropped, and `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` goes up. `link.expired` is sent the same way. See docs/webhooks.md.
7. `internal/api` answers with JSON. Errors carry an `error` field: 400 for an invalid body, 401 for a missing, wrong, or revoked key, 403 for a scope that doesn't allow the request, 409 for a slug in use, 429 for the rate limit.

## Logging

Every request, redirect or API, produces one line with `log_format` (JSON by default): `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `client_ip`, `request_id`. An incoming `X-Request-ID` header is used as the `request_id`; otherwise shortlink makes one and returns it in the same header.

# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

# Security

## TLS at the proxy

shortlink serves plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and point clients at the proxy. See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

When shortlink runs behind a proxy, every request appears to come from the proxy's address unless you tell it otherwise. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. That address is what rate limiting and request logs use, so only trust proxies you control.

## API keys

Create keys only on the server, with the narrowest scope that works:

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

A key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash, so a lost key cannot be recovered; create a new one and revoke the old one with `shortlink keys revoke <id>`. Treat keys like passwords: pass them in the Authorization header and keep them out of source control and shell history.

Scopes are read (GET requests), write (also create and delete links), and admin (also read every link's clicks across the server). A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

The admin password is separate from API keys. Set it with `shortlink admin set-password`, which stores its hash; a login lasts 12 hours.

## Target URLs

Targets must be http or https URLs no longer than max_url_length (2048 bytes). Refuse whole domains when you create links by listing them in blocked_domains; a link to one of those domains is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked". The check runs when a link is created, so review blocked_domains before importing links in bulk with `shortlink links import`.

The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved and can't be used as slugs. A slug already in use gets 409 Conflict.

With redirect_status 302 (the default), deleting a link or letting it expire stops the redirect at once. With 301, browsers cache the target and keep going there even after the link is deleted or expires. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## Metrics and the admin page

Prometheus metrics are served on metrics_addr (`:9090` by default), on a separate port from listen_addr. Keep that port off the public internet: bind it to a private interface or block it at the firewall. Set metrics_addr to an empty value to turn metrics off.

The admin page is off by default (admin.enabled false). It is read-only, but it shows links and their daily clicks, so put it behind the proxy's access controls as well as its own password. It is served on listen_addr under /admin.

## Webhook signing

If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. See docs/webhooks.md for the event payloads.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

messages.content:
# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

# Architecture

## Code layout

shortlink is one binary. Each part of it lives in its own package under `internal/`, except for the entry point:

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/shortlink` | Entry point. Parses the command line, loads configuration, opens the database, applies migrations, and starts the server. `shortlink` with no command runs `shortlink serve`. |
| `internal/store` | SQLite storage. Owns the `links`, `clicks_daily`, `api_keys`, and `schema_version` tables and the database file (`shortlink.db` by default) in WAL mode. |
| `internal/redirect` | Resolves short codes and answers redirects with `redirect_status`, applying `append_query` to the target. |
| `internal/api` | The JSON API under `/api`, and the request checks that go with it: URL length, `blocked_domains`, slug rules. |
| `internal/limit` | Per-client rate limiting: `rate_limit.requests_per_minute` with `rate_limit.burst` on top. |
| `internal/clicks` | Click counting. Holds counts in memory and writes them to `clicks_daily`. |
| `internal/hooks` | Webhooks: signing, delivery, and retries. |
| `internal/admin` | The read-only admin page served at `/admin`. |

The same process also answers `/healthz` and, on `metrics_addr`, `/metrics`. Migrations run automatically when the server starts; `shortlink migrate` applies them by hand.

## A redirect request

1. `internal/limit` rates the client. The client address comes from the connection, or from the `X-Forwarded-For` header when the peer is listed in `trusted_proxies` (see docs/deploy.md). Over the limit returns 429 and increments `shortlink_rate_limited_total`.
2. `internal/redirect` looks the code up in the in-memory cache, if `cache_size` is not 0. A hit adds to `shortlink_cache_hits_total`, a miss to `shortlink_cache_misses_total`, and the miss falls through to the database.
3. `internal/store` returns the link. A missing code, a reserved code (`api`, `admin`, `healthz`, `metrics`), or a link past its `expires_at` returns 404.
4. `internal/redirect` answers with `redirect_status` (302 by default) and, with `append_query` true, copies the short URL's query string onto the target. A `HEAD` request gets the same answer as `GET` but goes no further: no click is counted.
5. `internal/clicks` adds one click to its in-memory counts, bots included. Counts are written to `clicks_daily` every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds), so a new click appears in the API within about 5 seconds and a crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts. A normal shutdown flushes first.

## An API request

1. `internal/limit` rates the client as for a redirect.
2. `internal/api` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header and asks `internal/store` to match it against the `api_keys` table. The store compares the SHA-256 hash of the presented key. A missing, wrong, or revoked key is 401; a valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request is 403.
3. The key's scope decides what is allowed: `read` for GET, `write` for creating and deleting links, `admin` for reading every link's clicks across the server.
4. The handler validates the body in `internal/api`: targets must be `http` or `https` and no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), a domain in `blocked_domains` is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked", a `slug` is 3 to 32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens, and a slug already in use is 409 Conflict. Codes are generated by the store at `code_length` from letters and digits, minus `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, and `I`.
5. `internal/store` writes or reads the link. A link's target cannot be changed: delete it and create it again with the same slug.
6. For `link.created` and `link.deleted`, `internal/hooks` POSTs a JSON body to `webhooks.url` when that setting is set. Each request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. Delivery failures are retried up to 5 attempts in all, waiting 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s between them; after the last failure the event is logged and dropped, and `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` goes up. `link.expired` is sent the same way. See docs/webhooks.md.
7. `internal/api` answers with JSON. Errors carry an `error` field: 400 for an invalid body, 401 for a missing, wrong, or revoked key, 403 for a scope that doesn't allow the request, 409 for a slug in use, 429 for the rate limit.

## Logging

Every request, redirect or API, produces one line with `log_format` (JSON by default): `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `client_ip`, `request_id`. An incoming `X-Request-ID` header is used as the `request_id`; otherwise shortlink makes one and returns it in the same header.

# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

# Security

## TLS at the proxy

shortlink serves plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and point clients at the proxy. See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

When shortlink runs behind a proxy, every request appears to come from the proxy's address unless you tell it otherwise. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. That address is what rate limiting and request logs use, so only trust proxies you control.

## API keys

Create keys only on the server, with the narrowest scope that works:

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

A key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash, so a lost key cannot be recovered; create a new one and revoke the old one with `shortlink keys revoke <id>`. Treat keys like passwords: pass them in the Authorization header and keep them out of source control and shell history.

Scopes are read (GET requests), write (also create and delete links), and admin (also read every link's clicks across the server). A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

The admin password is separate from API keys. Set it with `shortlink admin set-password`, which stores its hash; a login lasts 12 hours.

## Target URLs

Targets must be http or https URLs no longer than max_url_length (2048 bytes). Refuse whole domains when you create links by listing them in blocked_domains; a link to one of those domains is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked". The check runs when a link is created, so review blocked_domains before importing links in bulk with `shortlink links import`.

The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved and can't be used as slugs. A slug already in use gets 409 Conflict.

With redirect_status 302 (the default), deleting a link or letting it expire stops the redirect at once. With 301, browsers cache the target and keep going there even after the link is deleted or expires. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## Metrics and the admin page

Prometheus metrics are served on metrics_addr (`:9090` by default), on a separate port from listen_addr. Keep that port off the public internet: bind it to a private interface or block it at the firewall. Set metrics_addr to an empty value to turn metrics off.

The admin page is off by default (admin.enabled false). It is read-only, but it shows links and their daily clicks, so put it behind the proxy's access controls as well as its own password. It is served on listen_addr under /admin.

## Webhook signing

If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. See docs/webhooks.md for the event payloads.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

# FAQ

## Why does shortlink use SQLite?

All links live in one SQLite file, shortlink.db by default, in WAL mode. There is no separate database server to install or keep in step with shortlink, and a backup is one command while the server runs:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

See deploy.md for backup notes.

## Can shortlink use Postgres?

No. Storage is SQLite only, in a single file set by the database setting. Other databases are not supported. Run one process per database file.

## Can I change where a link points?

No. A link's target is fixed when the link is created. To repoint a short code, delete the link and create it again with the same slug:

```sh
shortlink links delete x7Kp2
shortlink links add https://example.com/new/path --slug x7Kp2
```

Deleting first matters: a slug already in use gets 409 Conflict. The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved. Note that after a redirect_status of 301, browsers that already visited the link may keep going to the old target (see below).

## Are clicks unique visitors?

No. Each redirect counts one click, bots included. The counts tell you how often a short URL was followed, not how many different people followed it. Daily counts per link are kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days). HEAD requests are answered like GET but do not count a click.

## Why does a link still redirect after I deleted it?

If redirect_status is 301, browsers cache the redirect and keep going to the old target even after the link is deleted or expires. 302 (the default) is not cached that way. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## How soon do clicks show up?

Within about 5 seconds. Clicks are held in memory and written to the database every clicks.flush_interval (5s by default), so a new click appears in the API after roughly that long. A crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts; a normal shutdown writes them first. GET /api/links/{code} in api.md returns a link's total clicks.

## How do I run more than one server process?

Run one process per database file. Two shortlink processes sharing one SQLite file fail with "database is locked". Give each process its own database setting and its own file. If you are running shortlink behind a reverse proxy, see deploy.md for trusted_proxies, and see troubleshooting.md for the locked-database error.

## Where do I report a security problem?

Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

# Installing shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. It needs a SQLite file for its database and serves plain HTTP; TLS is terminated at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy (see deploy.md).

## Release binaries

Download the archive for your platform from the releases page. Binaries are published for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and darwin/arm64. Unpack it somewhere on the server and run the binary directly or under a process supervisor such as systemd.

## go install

With Go 1.26 or later installed:

```sh
go install example.com/shortlink/cmd/shortlink@latest
```

This puts `shortlink` in your Go binary directory.

## Container image

The image is `shortlink/shortlink`. It keeps its database in the `/data` volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` and mount the volume, or the database disappears with the container:

```sh
docker run --name shortlink -p 8080:8080 \
  -v shortlink-data:/data \
  -e DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db \
  shortlink/shortlink
```

Any setting can be given as an environment variable of the same name in capitals, with dots turned into underscores. `rate_limit.burst` becomes `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`; `database` becomes `DATABASE`, as above.

## First run

Copy `config/defaults.yaml` next to the binary and check the configuration before starting anything:

```sh
shortlink check-config
```

It loads the configuration, reports errors, and exits. Fix anything it points out, then start the server:

```sh
shortlink serve
```

`shortlink` with no command does the same thing as `shortlink serve`.

The settings you are most likely to change on a first run:

| Setting | Default | Change it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | the port is taken |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | the server is reachable under a public address |
| database | shortlink.db | the SQLite file belongs somewhere else |

`base_url` is the start of every short URL shortlink hands out, so set it to the address people will actually use. The database is one SQLite file; run one process per database file.

## Checking it works

The health check is at /healthz. Ask for it on the listen port:

```sh
curl -i http://localhost:8080/healthz
```

If the server answers, it is up and taking requests. Your first short URL is `base_url` plus the short code; with the defaults, a link with the code `x7Kp2` is `http://localhost:8080/x7Kp2`.

Metrics are served separately on `metrics_addr` (`:9090` by default), which keeps `/metrics` off the public port.

Create your first link with the CLI or the JSON API (see docs/api.md):

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path
```

If something does not behave as expected, see docs/troubleshooting.md. For backups and reverse proxy setup, see docs/deploy.md.

messages.content:
# Logging

shortlink writes one log line per request. Since v1.1.0 the default is
JSON (`log_format` json); earlier logs were text. Both formats carry
the same fields.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| log_format | json | `json` or `text` |
| log_level | info | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error` |

Set them in config/defaults.yaml or override with environment
variables: `LOG_FORMAT=text`, `LOG_LEVEL=debug`.

## Request log fields

Each request line has these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| method | HTTP method of the request |
| path | Request path |
| status | Response status code |
| duration_ms | Time taken to answer, in milliseconds |
| client_ip | Client address, from X-Forwarded-For when the request comes from a trusted proxy (see deploy.md) |
| request_id | ID of the request, see below |

A JSON line looks like this:

```json
{"method":"GET","path":"/x7Kp2","status":302,"duration_ms":2,"client_ip":"203.0.113.9","request_id":"a1b2c3d4"}
```

The text format prints the same fields on one line, for reading in a
terminal when you set `LOG_FORMAT=text`.

## Request IDs

Every request has a request ID. If the client sends an X-Request-ID
header, shortlink uses its value as the request_id in the log line. If
there is no such header, shortlink makes one and returns it in the
X-Request-ID response header, so the value is in the log either way.

Pass an ID you generate yourself when you want to follow one request
through a proxy, shortlink, and anything else that logs it. The same
ID appears in shortlink's log line and in the header you sent or
received.

## Levels

`log_level` sets the lowest level logged: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or
`error`. Request lines are logged at `info`, so with the default
`log_level` info every request is logged. Set `LOG_LEVEL=warn` to log
warnings and errors only.

## Related

- Metrics live on a separate port, metrics_addr (`:9090` by default);
  see docs/metrics.md.
- Webhook delivery failures are logged and counted in
  `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` (see webhooks.md).
- Shutdown behavior is covered in docs/performance.md: a normal stop
  writes pending click counts before the process exits.

# The database

shortlink keeps everything in one SQLite file. The `database` setting
names it (`shortlink.db` by default) and can be overridden with the
`DATABASE` environment variable. The container image keeps its database
in the /data volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` there. SQLite
runs in WAL mode. All storage goes through `internal/store`.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |

## Tables

| Table | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| links | Every link: its short code, target URL, creation time, and expiry time |
| clicks_daily | Daily click counts per link, kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days by default) |
| api_keys | API keys by name and scope, plus revocation state and each key's SHA-256 hash |
| schema_version | Which migrations have been applied to this file |

Only the hash of an API key is stored, never the key itself. A link's
target cannot be changed after the link is created; delete the link and
create it again with the same slug.

## Migrations

Since v1.3.0 migrations run automatically when the server starts. The
`shortlink migrate` command applies them by hand and exits:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Use it to migrate without starting the server, and when upgrading from
v1.2.0 or earlier: those databases predate automatic migrations, so run
`shortlink migrate` with the new binary before starting it.

Migrations only go forward. Downgrading after a migration is not
supported; restore a backup instead. Back up before every upgrade.

## One process per database file

Run one shortlink process per database file. A second process pointed at
the same file fails with "database is locked". If you need more than one
instance, give each its own `database` file.

## Supported databases

SQLite is the only supported database. The file named by `database` is
the whole datastore.

messages.content:
# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

# Security

## TLS at the proxy

shortlink serves plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and point clients at the proxy. See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

When shortlink runs behind a proxy, every request appears to come from the proxy's address unless you tell it otherwise. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. That address is what rate limiting and request logs use, so only trust proxies you control.

## API keys

Create keys only on the server, with the narrowest scope that works:

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

A key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash, so a lost key cannot be recovered; create a new one and revoke the old one with `shortlink keys revoke <id>`. Treat keys like passwords: pass them in the Authorization header and keep them out of source control and shell history.

Scopes are read (GET requests), write (also create and delete links), and admin (also read every link's clicks across the server). A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

The admin password is separate from API keys. Set it with `shortlink admin set-password`, which stores its hash; a login lasts 12 hours.

## Target URLs

Targets must be http or https URLs no longer than max_url_length (2048 bytes). Refuse whole domains when you create links by listing them in blocked_domains; a link to one of those domains is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked". The check runs when a link is created, so review blocked_domains before importing links in bulk with `shortlink links import`.

The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved and can't be used as slugs. A slug already in use gets 409 Conflict.

With redirect_status 302 (the default), deleting a link or letting it expire stops the redirect at once. With 301, browsers cache the target and keep going there even after the link is deleted or expires. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## Metrics and the admin page

Prometheus metrics are served on metrics_addr (`:9090` by default), on a separate port from listen_addr. Keep that port off the public internet: bind it to a private interface or block it at the firewall. Set metrics_addr to an empty value to turn metrics off.

The admin page is off by default (admin.enabled false). It is read-only, but it shows links and their daily clicks, so put it behind the proxy's access controls as well as its own password. It is served on listen_addr under /admin.

## Webhook signing

If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. See docs/webhooks.md for the event payloads.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

I can't see your live config from here, but here's what the docs say is required for rate limiting to work correctly behind a proxy — check your setup against these points:

**The one thing that must be right: `trusted_proxies`**

Per `docs/deploy.md` and `docs/security.md`, shortlink serves plain HTTP and normally sits behind a reverse proxy like nginx or Caddy. Without help, every request appears to come from the proxy's address, so **all your users share a single rate limit** (120 requests/minute plus a burst of 20 by default — see `docs/rate-limits.md`). That's the exact symptom described in `docs/troubleshooting.md` under "Every user hits the rate limit at once."

To fix/verify it, your config must list the proxy's address in `trusted_proxies` (default is `(none)` — so if you never set it, it's misconfigured). Example via env var, per `docs/configuration.md` (`rate_limit.burst` → `RATE_LIMIT_BURST` style):

```sh
TRUSTED_PROXIES=<your proxy's address>
```

Then run `shortlink check-config` to confirm the configuration loads without errors.

**Two caveats:**

1. **Only list proxies you control** (`docs/security.md`). Once a proxy is trusted, shortlink believes the `X-Forwarded-For` header it forwards — and that address is what rate limiting and request logs use. If you trust an address you don't control, a client can spoof its IP and evade rate limits.
2. **Redirects count too** (`docs/rate-limits.md`). Even with correct per-client limits, a link shared widely from one office network can exhaust that network's limit, since everyone there may appear from the same public IP.

**How to confirm it's working:** with `trusted_proxies` set, request logs should show individual client addresses rather than the proxy's address, and users should stop hitting 429s simultaneously. A client over the limit gets `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.

Also worth knowing: rate limits are tuned with `rate_limit.requests_per_minute` (default 120) and `rate_limit.burst` (default 20), overridable as `RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE` and `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`.

If you tell me your proxy address and what your config currently sets for `trusted_proxies`, I can tell you definitively whether it's right.

*Sources: `docs/deploy.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/rate-limits.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`*

messages.content:
# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

# Rate limits

Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

A client over its limit gets 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After
header giving the number of seconds to wait. Redirects count against
the limit too, so a link shared widely from one office network can
exhaust that network's limit.

# Troubleshooting

## A new link returns 404

If the link was created with an expires_at time that has already
passed, it is expired from the moment it is created, and its short URL
returns 404. Check the expires_at value, including its time zone.

## Every user hits the rate limit at once

shortlink is probably behind a proxy and sees every request as coming
from the proxy's address. Set trusted_proxies; see deploy.md.

## "database is locked"

Two shortlink processes are using the same SQLite file. Run one process
per database file.

messages.content:
# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

Use the **`trusted_proxies`** setting (env var `TRUSTED_PROXIES`) and set it to your proxy's address:

```
trusted_proxies: 10.0.0.2
```

As explained in `docs/deploy.md`, when shortlink sits behind a reverse proxy every request appears to come from the proxy's address, which collapses all users into one shared rate limit. Listing the proxy in `trusted_proxies` makes shortlink trust the `X-Forwarded-For` header it adds and take the real client address from there. The setting is described in `docs/configuration.md` as "Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed," with an empty default.

You can verify it loads correctly before restarting the server with `shortlink check-config` (also per `docs/configuration.md`).

Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

passed, it is expired from the moment it is created, and its short URL
returns 404. Check the expires_at value, including its time zone.

# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.

errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |

| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |

| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

```

```

messages.content:
# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

messages.content:
# Security

## TLS at the proxy

shortlink serves plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and point clients at the proxy. See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

When shortlink runs behind a proxy, every request appears to come from the proxy's address unless you tell it otherwise. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. That address is what rate limiting and request logs use, so only trust proxies you control.

## API keys

Create keys only on the server, with the narrowest scope that works:

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

A key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash, so a lost key cannot be recovered; create a new one and revoke the old one with `shortlink keys revoke <id>`. Treat keys like passwords: pass them in the Authorization header and keep them out of source control and shell history.

Scopes are read (GET requests), write (also create and delete links), and admin (also read every link's clicks across the server). A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

The admin password is separate from API keys. Set it with `shortlink admin set-password`, which stores its hash; a login lasts 12 hours.

## Target URLs

Targets must be http or https URLs no longer than max_url_length (2048 bytes). Refuse whole domains when you create links by listing them in blocked_domains; a link to one of those domains is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked". The check runs when a link is created, so review blocked_domains before importing links in bulk with `shortlink links import`.

The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved and can't be used as slugs. A slug already in use gets 409 Conflict.

With redirect_status 302 (the default), deleting a link or letting it expire stops the redirect at once. With 301, browsers cache the target and keep going there even after the link is deleted or expires. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## Metrics and the admin page

Prometheus metrics are served on metrics_addr (`:9090` by default), on a separate port from listen_addr. Keep that port off the public internet: bind it to a private interface or block it at the firewall. Set metrics_addr to an empty value to turn metrics off.

The admin page is off by default (admin.enabled false). It is read-only, but it shows links and their daily clicks, so put it behind the proxy's access controls as well as its own password. It is served on listen_addr under /admin.

## Webhook signing

If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. See docs/webhooks.md for the event payloads.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

messages.content:
# The database

shortlink keeps everything in one SQLite file. The `database` setting
names it (`shortlink.db` by default) and can be overridden with the
`DATABASE` environment variable. The container image keeps its database
in the /data volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` there. SQLite
runs in WAL mode. All storage goes through `internal/store`.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |

## Tables

| Table | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| links | Every link: its short code, target URL, creation time, and expiry time |
| clicks_daily | Daily click counts per link, kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days by default) |
| api_keys | API keys by name and scope, plus revocation state and each key's SHA-256 hash |
| schema_version | Which migrations have been applied to this file |

Only the hash of an API key is stored, never the key itself. A link's
target cannot be changed after the link is created; delete the link and
create it again with the same slug.

## Migrations

Since v1.3.0 migrations run automatically when the server starts. The
`shortlink migrate` command applies them by hand and exits:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Use it to migrate without starting the server, and when upgrading from
v1.2.0 or earlier: those databases predate automatic migrations, so run
`shortlink migrate` with the new binary before starting it.

Migrations only go forward. Downgrading after a migration is not
supported; restore a backup instead. Back up before every upgrade.

## One process per database file

Run one shortlink process per database file. A second process pointed at
the same file fails with "database is locked". If you need more than one
instance, give each its own `database` file.

## Supported databases

SQLite is the only supported database. The file named by `database` is
the whole datastore.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file, but copying it directly can catch
it partway through a write. Back it up with the SQLite backup command
while the server runs:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

Back up the database before every upgrade, and before running
`shortlink migrate` by hand. If an upgrade or a migration has to be
undone, stop the server and put the backup back in place as the database
file; run one process per database file as usual.

# The admin page

The admin page is a read-only view of the links in the database. It is
off by default and lives at /admin on `listen_addr` (`:8080` by
default). It arrived in v1.4.0.

## Turning it on

Set `admin.enabled` in config/defaults.yaml, or override it with an
environment variable of the same name in capitals:

```yaml
admin:
  enabled: true
```

```sh
ADMIN_ENABLED=true shortlink serve
```

Run `shortlink check-config` to confirm the configuration loads.

## Setting the password

`admin.password_hash` is not written by hand. Run this on the server
and enter the password at the prompt:

```sh
shortlink admin set-password
```

The command stores the hash in `admin.password_hash`. shortlink keeps
only the hash, so the password cannot be recovered from the
configuration. Run the command again to change the password.

## What it shows

Everything on the page is read-only. You can:

- Search links.
- See each link's daily click counts.

You cannot create, edit, or delete links there. To change links, use
the JSON API or the `shortlink links` commands; see api.md. Daily click
counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default), so the
page does not show counts older than that.

## Logging in

Sign in with the password set by `shortlink admin set-password`. A login
lasts 12 hours, after which you sign in again.

## Protecting /admin

The page is served on `listen_addr` under /admin, the same port as
redirects and the API, so it is reachable wherever that port is
reachable. Put it behind the access controls of your reverse proxy as
well, for example HTTP basic auth or an IP allowlist in nginx or Caddy.
See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

If you also run shortlink behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For,
list the proxy in `trusted_proxies` so rate limiting sees the real
client address.

## Example

```yaml
listen_addr: :8080
database: shortlink.db
admin:
  enabled: true
  password_hash: "$2a$10$..."   # set by `shortlink admin set-password`
```

Then start the server and open http://localhost:8080/admin.

# Configuration

shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |

# Rate limits

Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

A client over its limit gets 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After
header giving the number of seconds to wait. Redirects count against
the limit too, so a link shared widely from one office network can
exhaust that network's limit.

messages.content:
# Deploying shortlink

shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

## Behind a reverse proxy

When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

## Backups

The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.
